title: Descent and smooth normalization of the lci cotangent determinant
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and fix $d\geq0$. Suppose $X$ has an open cover by factorizations $U\xrightarrow{i}P\to S$, where $P$ is open in $\mathbf A^n_S$ and $i$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose ideal $I$ is locally generated by a Koszul-regular sequence of length $c=n-d$ [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Assume $C_i=I/I^2$, regarded on $U$, is locally free of rank $c$. Put $V_i=i^*\Omega^1_{P/S}$, $E_i=[C_i\xrightarrow{\mathrm d}V_i]$ in degrees $-1,0$, and $D_i=(\bigwedge^c C_i)^\vee\otimes\bigwedge^nV_i$, with $\vee=\mathcal Hom(-,\mathcal O_U)$. Pullbacks, differentials, exterior powers and sheaf duals use [def-pc-module-pullback, def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf, def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power, def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Let $L=L_{X/S}$ with its canonical conormal comparisons $\lambda_i:E_i\simeq L|_U$ be the cotangent complex of [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation], and use the determinant functor of [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant] with its affine-local normalization: its exterior-model comparisons commute with restriction to open subschemes, and on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R$, for a degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphism $a:P\to Q$ between two-term complexes of finite projective $R$-modules, $\det(a)$ is, under the exterior-model comparisons, the kernel-normalized map $T_a$ of [lem-trf-surjective-two-term-determinant-calculus] (the ordinary tensor symmetry reorders the two factors). Then $L$ is perfect of Tor amplitude $[-1,0]$ globally and $D=\det L$ is an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Every $C_i$ and $V_i$ has the stated constant ranks $c,n$, and the exterior-model comparison gives a canonical $\alpha_i:D_i\xrightarrow{\sim}D|_U$. The transitions $t_{ij}=\alpha_j^{-1}\alpha_i$ are independent of the chosen polynomial presentations, commute with restriction and refinement, and satisfy $t_{ii}=1$ and $t_{jk}t_{ij}=t_{ik}$ on every overlap. No separatedness of $X/S$ or affineness of overlaps is assumed. On every open $T\subset X$ where $f$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], $\Omega^1_{T/S}$ has rank $d$ and the canonical map $L|_T\simeq\Omega^1_{T/S}[0]$ induces $D|_T\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigwedge^d\Omega^1_{T/S}$. This isomorphism agrees with the local exact-conormal-sequence determinant comparison, using the relation-first wedge order, and with the maps $\alpha_i$ on all smooth overlaps.

source.place: Tag 0FJX (lemma-determinant-two-term-complexes), applied to cotangent.tex Tag 08SL (proposition-cotangent-complex-local-complete-intersection); smooth rank and normalization: morphisms.tex Tag 02G1 (lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free), cotangent.tex Tag 08R5 (lemma-when-projective).

proof.text: Work locally over affine opens of $S$ and then on principal opens of the ambient affine space. The polynomial differential basis and its localization identify $\Omega^1_{P/S}$ with $\mathcal O_P^n$, with basis $\mathrm dx_1,\ldots,\mathrm dx_n$. The definition of the differential sheaf identifies these affine descriptions. Pulling the basis back gives $V_i\simeq\mathcal O_U^n$. The rank $c$ of $C_i$ is an explicit hypothesis, so both terms of $E_i$ are finite locally free with the required ranks; no rank assertion is inferred from the number of equations alone.

Use the canonical conormal isomorphisms $\lambda_i:E_i\simeq L|_{U_i}$ supplied by the cotangent-presentation node. Since these opens cover $X$, they exhibit $L$ locally as a two-term finite locally free complex, precisely the local criterion for perfect Tor amplitude $[-1,0]$ in the determinant node. Apply that node on $X$ to obtain the invertible line $D=\det L$. Its exterior-model comparison, followed by $\det(\lambda_i)$ and the inverse of the restriction comparison $D|_{U_i}\simeq\det(L|_{U_i})$, defines $\alpha_i:D_i\simeq D|_{U_i}$.

On an arbitrary overlap define $t_{ij}=\alpha_j^{-1}\alpha_i$. Cancellation gives $t_{ii}=1$ and $t_{jk}t_{ij}=\alpha_k^{-1}\alpha_j\alpha_j^{-1}\alpha_i=t_{ik}$. For a third presentation, its comparison is likewise the composite through $D$; consequently inserting it into a comparison does not change the result. This is the precise independence of presentations, rather than an equality of the different model lines. The conormal comparisons respect restriction, the exterior-model comparisons commute with restriction by the normalization fixed in the statement, and determinant pullback respects isomorphisms and compositions, so restricting any $\alpha_i$ or $t_{ij}$ gives the comparison on the restricted presentation. The same cancellation proves compatibility with successive refinements. All these are maps of sheaves on the overlaps themselves; intersections of affines need not be affine.

source.place: Tags 0FJX and 0FJY, functoriality and restriction comparisons.

proof.text: On a smooth open $T$, the canonical augmentation $a:L|_T\simeq\Omega^1_{T/S}[0]$ is an isomorphism by the cotangent-presentation node, and $W=\Omega^1_{T/S}$ is finite locally free by the smooth-differentials node. On $U_i\cap T$ the composite $a\lambda_i$ is the augmentation $q:[C_i\xrightarrow{d}V_i]\to W[0]$: its degree-zero map sends an ambient differential to its differential on $T$, as in the natural conormal comparison. Thus $H^{-1}(E_i)=\ker d=0$ and $H^0(E_i)=\operatorname{coker}d=W$, giving $0\to C_i\to V_i\to W\to0$. Locally choose a basis of $W$ and lift its finitely many elements through the surjection $V_i\to W$; together with a local basis of $C_i$ this gives a basis of $V_i$. Comparing lengths yields $\operatorname{rank}W=n-c=d$. The determinant functor applied to $a$, followed by the exterior-model comparison for $[0\to W]$, defines $\beta:D|_T\simeq\bigwedge^d W$.

source.place: Tag 08R5 (lemma-when-projective); morphisms.tex Tag 02G1 (lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free); perfect.tex Tags 0FJX and 0FJY.

proof.text:
Compute $\beta\alpha_i$ on affine opens of $U_i\cap T$ where $C_i,W$ are free. These form a cover even when $U_i\cap T$ is not affine. The augmentation $q:[C_i\to V_i]\to[0\to W]$ is a degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphism of finite free complexes. By the affine-local normalization fixed in the statement (realized by the affine determinant system, whose derived isomorphisms act by kernel-normalized good-diagram maps), $\det(q)$ is the map $T_q$ of the surjective two-term determinant calculus. Its kernel is $[C_i\xrightarrow{d}dC_i]$. For a basis $c_1,\ldots,c_c$ of $C_i$, the differential sends it to the basis $dc_1,\ldots,dc_c$ of $dC_i$, so its determinant trivialization is $(c_1\wedge\cdots\wedge c_c)^\vee\otimes(dc_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dc_c)$. The degree-zero short-exact-sequence map in that calculus wedges kernel elements first and quotient lifts second; the degree-minus-one map identifies $C_i$ with its kernel. Therefore $\det(q)$ sends
$$(c_1\wedge\cdots\wedge c_c)^\vee\otimes(dc_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dc_c\wedge\widetilde w_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\widetilde w_d)$$
to $w_1\wedge\cdots\wedge w_d$. Functoriality gives $\beta\alpha_i=\det(a\lambda_i)=\det(q)$ under the exterior comparisons. This proves exactly the relation-first normalization, without a sign from permuting the two blocks. Since the computed map is the already defined sheaf morphism $\beta\alpha_i$, the equality holds globally once checked on this affine cover.

source.place: Tag 0FJI (section-determinants-complexes), degreewise-surjective quasi-isomorphism construction before 0FJJ; Tag 0FJM; perfect.tex Tag 0FJX.

proof.text: On a smooth overlap the two exact-conormal determinant comparisons are $\beta\alpha_i$ and $\beta\alpha_j$. Hence $(\beta\alpha_j)t_{ij}=\beta\alpha_j\alpha_j^{-1}\alpha_i=\beta\alpha_i$. This proves their compatibility with every transition. Restrictions of $\beta$ are obtained from the same canonical augmentation and determinant restriction comparison, so the smooth identifications also agree on overlapping smooth opens. For $c=0$ or $d=0$, the calculation uses the empty wedge $1$ and the same equations; the empty scheme imposes no local rank condition.

source.place: Tags 0FJX and 0FJY; elementary composition of the maps constructed in the preceding steps.
